title: Customer SLA-fingerprint intake and GPU-fit decision flow
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Why: Sales and Solutions Engineering are regularly fielding requests for reserved throughput with incomplete signals (e.g., ‘we need low latency’). Lack of a consistent, repeatable intake and decision flow causes over-provisioning, SLA mismatches, and slow sales cycles.

Goal: Ship an intake + decision flow that produces a compact ‘SLA fingerprint’ for each customer request and maps that fingerprint to a recommended reserved-throughput profile, GPU class, and rollout guardrails. The output must be machine-readable (for automation) and human-reviewable (for concessions by Solutions Eng).

Scope: This ticket covers the product definition, scorecard weights, and rollout decision guidance. Implementation tasks (form + scoring service + Console UI) are tracked in follow-ups with ENG. Excludes billing model changes and contract generation language (handled by finance/legal).
acceptance_criteria: A documented SLA-fingerprint schema that captures: 99p latency target, median latency target, sustained RPS, burst RPS, availability target, retry budget, cost sensitivity, region/residency constraints, and security requirements.
A deterministic scoring rubric (0-100) with clear weightings and explanation for each input dimension.
A mapping table from score bands to recommended reserved-throughput buckets and GPU class with example tuning knobs (batching, quantization recommendations, KV cache hints).
Rollout guidance for each band (canary %, canary duration, fallback policy, burst credit allowance) included and reviewable by Solutions Eng.
Stakeholder signoff captured from Sales, Solutions Eng, Runtime Eng, and Legal (privacy/residency constraints).
Linked Confluence page with examples from three recent enterprise intake requests and a sample completed intake form.
A lightweight handoff doc for Engineering with API contract for the scoring endpoint (inputs/outputs) and Console UX wireframes.

Measureable success criteria: reduce median sales-to-commit time for dedicated requests by 30% in pilot and reduce first-pass over-provisioning rate by 40% for pilot cohort (tracked in follow-up analytics).
discussion: 2026-02-22 — Kickoff w/ Sales + Solutions Eng. Common pain: incomplete traffic shape and vague latency goals. Agreed on 'SLA-fingerprint' concept. Action: PM to prototype schema.

2026-02-28 — Draft schema proposed. Trade-offs: include cost sensitivity as explicit field (helps map to quantization), but Sales worried it will complicate negotiations. Decision: include as optional enumerated field (low/medium/high) with default 'medium'.

2026-03-03 — Eng architecture sync. Proposal: scoring service returns numeric score + justification tokens (human-readable reasons). Eng asks to keep token list small (~3 reasons) to avoid UI clutter.
2026-03-05 — Design feedback: need Console pattern for quick override by Solutions Eng. Design to provide 'recommended profile' + 'override' with audit trail.

2026-03-09 — Scoring rubric consensus: weights = traffic shape (sustained RPS & burst) 30%, latency targets (99p & median) 25%, availability/region/residency 20%, security/compliance 15%, cost sensitivity 10%. Rationale: traffic shape drives throughput and GPU selection; latency drives model and kernel choices.

2026-03-12 — Draft mapping table agreed for pilot: score >= 85 => H100-class reserved (burst credit allowed, 5% canary for 72 hours); 70-84 => A100-80GB reserved (canary 5% for 48 hours); 50-69 => A10/A30 mixed pool with routing + auto-burst; <50 => hosted API + recommendation for integration work prior to Dedicated.
2026-03-13 — Risk note from Runtime Eng: H100 reservations are limited in APAC region. Action: scorer must surface region constraints and suggest fallback GPU families automatically.
2026-03-14 — Legal signoff pending on residency language. Solutions Eng wants sample SLA clause for inclusion in SOW templates. PM to coordinate with Legal (separate task).
notes: Implementation plan (high-level): 1) Finalize schema and mapping table; 2) Build intake form + Console UX; 3) Implement scoring service (stateless); 4) Add audit trail and 'override with justification' in Console; 5) Pilot with 5 enterprise customers via Solutions Eng.
Pilot measurement plan: instrument time-to-commit and provisioned-GPU mismatch rate in the analytics dashboard. Metrics owner: Growth Analytics (TBD).
Open questions: How strictly should the scorer be enforced vs advisory? (Current lean: advisory by default, can be enforced via triage policy).
Follow-ups created: ENG-INTAKE-43 (scoring service API), DES-INTAKE-12 (Console override UX), LEG-RES-7 (SOW residency clause).
